findings.summary: Validated StreamEvent payloads are re-cast in activeTurnReducer instead of staying narrowed downstream.
findings.invariant: Validate once at the public event trust boundary; downstream reducer code consumes trusted discriminated variants without reconstructing types by assertion.

findings.summary: activeTurnReducer is not exhaustive; legal variants can fall through default and not advance sequence bookkeeping.
findings.invariant: Every legal public event is either state-changing or an explicit no-op and all legal events preserve ordered sequence accounting.

findings.summary: Reducer tests can create StreamEvent values through casts that the production parser would reject.
findings.invariant: Protocol tests use type-directed builders or parser-backed fixtures and cannot claim coverage with impossible wire values.

findings.summary: Malformed model tool-call JSON is normalized to an empty object and can be emitted as a valid completed tool call.
findings.invariant: Invalid model output remains an explicit invalid/error state and is never executed as a valid tool call.

findings.summary: StreamEventFactory mutates caller-owned StreamEventIds while enriching identity.
findings.invariant: Factories return new values and do not introduce hidden aliasing through caller mutation.

findings.summary: ToolExecutor validation/normalization mutates caller-owned argument dictionaries.
findings.invariant: Validation is side-effect free; normalization returns an explicit new value.

findings.summary: Job.Status is a raw string instead of a finite domain type.
findings.invariant: Durable lifecycle state has one typed vocabulary shared by model, repository and service transitions.

findings.summary: Job runtime treats completed and succeeded as duplicate successful terminal states.
findings.invariant: One semantic state has one canonical spelling; successful Job terminal state is completed.

findings.summary: Job transition uses read-check-write rather than an invariant-bearing compare-and-set mutation.
findings.invariant: Concurrent lifecycle transitions cannot both succeed from the same expected state.

findings.summary: Authoritative Job lifecycle event append is best-effort after status mutation.
findings.invariant: When status and lifecycle event represent one durable fact they commit atomically.

findings.summary: Python internal runtime protocol and public StreamEvent reuse an overly generic event envelope/vocabulary.
findings.invariant: Internal Agent control/runtime protocol is distinct from Go-owned public projection protocol.

findings.summary: A fresh worktree root typecheck failed because ai-service:typecheck did not declare the OCR extra required by imported fitz/pytesseract modules.
findings.invariant: The root typecheck target is self-contained on a fresh worktree and does not depend on another command having preinstalled optional packages.
findings.verification: Removed apps/ai-service/.venv and ran pnpm typecheck; ai-service recreated the environment and pyright completed with 0 errors.

findings.summary: Web lint uses the deprecated @nx/eslint:lint executor and emits an Nx v24 migration warning.
findings.invariant: Quality gates use supported Nx target configuration without deprecation noise.

findings.summary: Passing Web unit tests emit repeated localhost:3000 ECONNREFUSED diagnostics and one React act warning.
findings.invariant: A green unit suite is quiet enough that new actionable warnings are visible.

findings.summary: Production build reports BodyExplorer3D chunk above the configured 500 kB warning threshold.
findings.invariant: Large intentional assets/chunks have an explicit loading/performance rationale or are split when that improves user-facing latency.
